title: Detector
description: One yes or no call that Naive makes on evidence, after signal detection theory (Green and Swets 1966), at <venture>/governance/detectors/<id>.json. It names the question, the sensor that scores the evidence, the criterion that turns a score into a call, its impact tier, the costs of the four outcomes, the base rate and who resolves each call. A detector names its sensor and never runs it. Every call is a trial in the detection ledger beside it (<id>.trials.jsonl, detector-trial.schema.json). Naive never moves a criterion by itself: a better one is proposed as an open decision and a person accepts it. Design: docs/design/SIGNAL_DETECTION_2026-11-07.md.

id.description: The detector's id, the same as its file name without .json.

call_site.description: Where the call is made, such as a module and the setting it reads, for example packages/naive/src/engine/gate.mjs confidence_below.

assign_to.description: Optional: the role a yes call is put to as an open decision, by id: a role in the roles registers or a role template (governance/roles/<id>.json). A seam detector names the lead whose portfolio spans the seam, such as finance-lead for tools against spend. It changes who is asked, not who decides: only a person settles the decision, and settling it resolves the call's trial.

tier.description: The impact tier of the question type, from operating-rules.json. It sets the default costs: low makes a miss and a false alarm cost the same, and costly makes a miss cost three times a false alarm. one_way_door has no criterion: every call goes to a person, the ledger still records each trial, and no criterion change is ever proposed.

question.description: The yes or no question, as a question type in operating-rules.json: a verb, a noun or a scoped noun, and the function that asks.

verb.description: What is asked about the noun, such as accept or hold.

noun.description: A noun from the ontology, or a scoped noun name@function.

asking_function.description: The id of the function that asks, from packages/naive/src/functions/departments.json.

text.description: The question in a plain sentence.

evidence.description: Where the signals come from, the sensor that turns them into a score, and the scale of that score. A higher score means more evidence for yes unless scale.yes_when is below.

kind.description: check: a deterministic check computes the score. founder-agent: the founder's own agent gives a confidence with its answer. person: a person rates on a scale. accumulated: a statistic over past outcomes. sequential: evidence added up over time until it crosses a boundary, as the standing rule's SPRT does.

sensor.description: What produces the score: a module path, a model step id, a role or a person, as the kind needs.

sources.description: Where the signals come from, so every score can be traced to the records it was read from. Signals reach Naive as records, so each entry names a source of the venture and the records read there.

source.description: A source id from the venture's knowledge/sources.json, or venture for the venture's own folder

records.description: The route of the records read there, such as product/bugs or evidence/[id]

scale.description: The range and meaning of the score. Leave out a bound the score has none on.

meaning.description: What the score is, such as a confidence from 0 to 1 or a log likelihood ratio.

yes_when.description: Which side of the yes line is yes, matching the call site's own comparison. above (the default): a score at or above yes is yes. below: a score strictly below yes is yes, as the gate holds a write whose confidence is below its line. Scores are never inverted with 1 - x, so a line keeps the exact number the call site compares against.

calibrated.description: True when the score is a likelihood ratio, so a criterion can be derived from the costs and the base rate by formula. A raw confidence from a model is not calibrated.

criterion.description: Where the line is drawn on the score scale, or route person when every call goes to a person. Under evidence.scale.yes_when above (the default): with yes alone, a score at or above it is a yes call and any other score is a no; with yes and no, a score at or above yes is yes, a score at or below no is no, a score between them is unsure and goes to a person, and no must be below yes. Under yes_when below the sides swap and the yes line is strict: a score below yes is yes, a score at or above no (or at or above yes when there is no no line) is no, and no must be above yes.

route.description: Every call goes to a person and no line is drawn. A one_way_door detector has this and nothing else.

costs.description: What each of the four outcomes is worth, as positive amounts on one scale: hit and correct_rejection are the value of a right call, miss and false_alarm the cost of a wrong one. By default they come from the tier: 1 for each at low, and at costly a miss costs 3 and the rest 1. A person may set others. A one_way_door detector has none.

hit.description: The value of saying yes when the answer was yes.

miss.description: The cost of saying no when the answer was yes.

false_alarm.description: The cost of saying yes when the answer was no.

correct_rejection.description: The value of saying no when the answer was no.

set_by.description: The person who set the costs, or tier when they are the tier's defaults.

decision.description: The decision that set the costs, if any.

base_rate.description: How often the true answer is yes.

source.description: stated: a person stated it in value. ledger: it is computed from the resolved trials in the ledger each time it is needed.

value.description: stated only: the proportion of calls whose true answer is yes.

set_by.description: stated only: the person who stated it.

resolution.description: Who settles whether a call was right, and how long to wait for it.

kind.description: person: a person decides, by name or role. record: a later record settles it, such as an accepted draft or a reverted write. producer: the code or agent that produced the judged write reports the outcome.

id.description: The person or role, the record type, or the producer.

time_to_detect.description: A number followed by s, m, h, d or w. A call with no resolution after this long counts as unresolved, not as right.

line.description: One criterion on the score scale.

set_by.description: The person who set it; derived when Naive derived it from the costs and the base rate and a person accepted it; or default when it is a default Naive ships in packages/naive/template/governance/detectors/, chosen by hand in Naive and not by a person of the venture. A venture that keeps its own copy names the person who set it.

decision.description: The decision that set or accepted it, if any.
